content.text: AI Breast Cancer Biomarker Classification from H&E Histology Images
An AI-enabled web triage tool predicts breast cancer biomarkers from routine H&E histology images to help pathology laboratories prioritize cases for further testing.

The system uses deep learning models trained on the IHC4BC dataset to predict the expression of ER, PR, Ki-67, and HER2 from routine H&E histology images. This enables rapid, accurate assessments of breast cancer biomarkers without the need for costly and time-consuming confirmatory testing.

content.text: Executive Summary

Pathology laboratories use biomarker results to inform breast cancer diagnosis and treatment planning, but conventional immunohistochemistry (IHC) testing can be costly, time-consuming and labor-intensive. This project applies AI to routine H&E images to predict ER, PR, Ki-67 and HER2, with the aim of supporting faster triage and reducing reliance on routine IHC panels. The case study describes a web application as ready for clinical validation; it does not establish routine clinical deployment or provide numerical diagnostic-performance results.

This solution not only supports pathologists by providing rapid, accurate predictions but also offers substantial cost savings by reducing the need for routine IHC panels.

Context and Challenge

For pathology teams, conventional biomarker assessment relies on IHC panels for ER, PR, Ki-67 and HER2. The case study identifies cost and processing time, the labor and expertise required for manual evaluation, and high case volumes as pressures on laboratory workflows. It also notes that variation in assessment quality can complicate consistency and quality assurance.

Cost and Time Constraints: Traditional IHC testing can be expensive and time-consuming, leading to delays in diagnosis and increasing healthcare costs. Labor-Intensive Process: Manual biomarker evaluation requires substantial labor and expertise, making it difficult to scale in high-volume clinical settings. Backlog in Pathology: Laboratories are often overwhelmed by large volumes of cases, leading to delays in processing and reporting, which can impact patient outcomes. Inconsistent Quality Control: The quality and consistency of manual assessments can vary, affecting the reliability of results and creating challenges in audits and quality assurance.

content.text: These constraints make it difficult to scale testing and can contribute to delays in processing and reporting. The documented project goal is to use AI predictions as a triage aid—not to claim that H&E predictions replace confirmatory testing or pathologist judgment.

content.text: Results and Business Impact

The case study presents prioritization for confirmatory testing and reduced reliance on routine IHC panels as the intended workflow value; no measured reduction or savings figure is supplied.

The Breast Cancer Biomarker Classification project represents a significant step forward in automating and streamlining breast cancer diagnosis. By reducing the need for expensive IHC panels, the platform offers substantial cost savings while improving the speed and consistency of biomarker assessments. With strong validation performance and an intuitive web app for integration, this solution is poised for clinical validation and adoption as a triage and decision-support tool in pathology workflows.

This project showcases the transformative potential of AI in healthcare, providing a clear path for scaling and clinical validation to enhance patient care while reducing the costs and workload for pathologists.

content.text: Conclusion

This project applies H&E-based AI predictions and a web triage workflow to a practical challenge for pathology laboratories: the cost and effort of conventional biomarker testing. The described capability provides a basis for evaluating case prioritization, but clinical validation and measurable laboratory impact remain to be established.
